title: Change Anything: The New Science of Personal Success
author: Kerry Patterson
Joseph Grenny
David Maxfield
Ron McMillan
Al Switzler
target_audience: Adults seeking to change habits or behaviors
Professionals working on career or productivity goals
Anyone struggling with lasting personal change (e.g., health, finances, relationships)
core_themes: Environmental and social influences on behavior
primary_purpose: To equip readers with evidence-based frameworks and practical tools for changing any persistent, self-limiting behavior by leveraging actionable strategies drawn from social science research.

structure_format.organization: Introduces a six-source model of influence and applies it through case studies, personal stories, and step-by-step guidance

key_concepts_lessons: Personal change fails when people rely solely on willpower without understanding the forces that influence behavior.
The 'Six Sources of Influence'—personal motivation, personal ability, social motivation, social ability, structural motivation, and structural ability—affect all change efforts.
Analyzing and altering your environment can drive or impede success.
Recruiting social support and accountability is crucial for sustained change.
Understanding triggers and designing effective strategies makes success more likely.
Systematic self-assessment and adjustment lead to long-term results.
notable_features: Six Sources of Influence model for behavior change
Uses concrete, research-backed examples across health, finances, relationships, and work
Step-by-step process to diagnose and overcome obstacles
Emphasizes analysis and customization over generic advice
cultural_historical_context: Published in the early 2010s, the book reflects a surge of interest in habit change and behavioral science popularized by contemporary research and books addressing psychology, productivity, and success.
reception_impact: Widely praised for its actionable content and interdisciplinary approach
Valued by coaches, business leaders, and therapists as a change management resource
Lauded for demystifying why change is hard and providing concrete steps to overcome setbacks
Embraced by readers struggling with personal or professional transformation
Some critics feel the case studies are repetitive or the framework requires commitment to fully implement
comparable_titles: Switch: How to Change Things When Change Is Hard by Chip Heath and Dan Heath
The Power of Habit by Charles Duhigg
Influencer: The New Science of Leading Change by Kerry Patterson, Joseph Grenny, et al.
